::: {#exm-bigram-model}

#### A bigram model of the training text

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
pair_counts = torch.ones(n_chars, n_chars)
_ = pair_counts.index_put_(
    (train_ids[:-1], train_ids[1:]), torch.ones(n_train - 1), accumulate=True
)
bigram = pair_counts / pair_counts.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
p_u_after_q = bigram[index["q"], index["u"]].item()
after_t = bigram[index["t"]]
top_after_t = chars[after_t.argmax().item()]
p_top_after_t = after_t.max().item()
print(p_u_after_q, repr(top_after_t), p_top_after_t)
```

`pair_counts` starts every count at 1 and adds the training pairs,
so row $a$ of `bigram` is the [bigram model](#def-bigram-model)'s distribution of the character after $a$.
Its most likely character after `t` is `r if (py$top_after_t == " ") "the space" else py$top_after_t`,
with probability `r sprintf("%.2f", py$p_top_after_t)`.
It gives a `u` after a `q` probability `r sprintf("%.2f", py$p_u_after_q)`,
against the share of `r sprintf("%.2f", py$share_u)` in @sol-after-q.
There are only `r py$n_q` `q`s to count,
so the `r py$n_chars` added ones are a large part of the row.

:::
